source.title: Geometry of Ordinal Representations in Language Models

record.file_problem: Whole paper text is present; there are minor extraction and formatting artifacts, but the findings and tables are readable.
record.tranche_reason: Applies manifold and feature-family analyses to ordinal tasks across three open-weight language models, extending prior counting-manifold work to new tasks and models. It does not test superposition or capacity pressure directly.
record.gate_note: Rows record the paper's own SAE feature-family results and ordinal-manifold dimensionality findings. Probe scores, twist scores, and activation-patching drops are not rows because they do not measure the claim versions' feature-capacity or dictionary-feature claims. Results cited from other work are excluded.
record.test_reason: This is a new setting: ordinal tasks in Gemma-2-2B/9B and Qwen3-4B. Its own Gemma Scope SAE feature-family counts bear on V4 (whether SAEs recover sparse features for these variables). Its PCA of per-value centroids bears on V6 (1-D versus multi-dimensional representation of a variable). The link is indirect. There is no baseline for SAE selectivity, and the dimensionality is measured on centroids rather than token-level features, which the authors stress. It does not test V1, V2, V3 or V5.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. One correction: the authors describe indentation as 2–3D (summarised as a 3D subspace), table rows as 1–4D depending on model, and numeric magnitude as 4–5D without clean manifold structure. They frame their taxonomy as tentative, based on four tasks.
record.recipe_differences: Studies ordinal-task centroid manifolds, SAE feature families, attention-head transformations, and subspace patching in open-weight LMs; it does not reproduce a toy-model superposition intervention or measure sparse-feature capacity.
record.method_sensitivity: Task and architecture change the reported geometry; bracket depth and table columns are described as 1D, whereas indentation, table rows, and numeric magnitude show higher-dimensional structure in some or all models. SAE feature-family analysis is limited to Gemma models because no pretrained SAE is available for Qwen3-4B.

fits_no_version.finding: SAE features discretize continuous ordinal manifolds as place-cell tilings. Several top features are shared value=0 'beginning of structure' detectors across tasks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE features can be tilings of a continuous manifold rather than the model's own units (relevant to V5/V6, not tested as such).

fits_no_version.finding: Patching the top-3 manifold directions drops probe accuracy far more than random directions (ratio >28×).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Ordinal information is concentrated in a low-dimensional subspace (informational, not behavioural).

record.peer_reviewed: Mechanistic Interpretability Workshop at the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, 2026
record.problems: The paper notes substantial bracket-depth probe overfitting (99% train accuracy versus 53–57% test accuracy), a minor synthetic bracket-labeling inconsistency, no pretrained Qwen3-4B SAE, and that PCA characterizes per-value centroids rather than individual-token concentration. The patching method tests informational concentration rather than behavioral causality. Some figure-specific dimensionality details are not stated numerically in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No reported results on the claim versions were left out. Twist-score, probe-score, and patching results were excluded because they do not directly measure these versions' capacity-pressure, polysemanticity, or dictionary-unit claims.

untested.parts: No toy models, no sparsity sweep, no overlapping-direction geometry.
Spread of features across neurons is not measured. There are no SAE results for Qwen3-4B.
Completeness, stability and canonicity of SAE features are not tested. Only a 16K Gemma Scope dictionary is used.
Dimensionality of individual (token-level or SAE) features is not measured, only centroid manifolds.

missing.what: Cross-task sharing of top SAE features in Gemma-2-2B (#9213, #15567, #7214, #6631 are value=0 detectors).
Per-model layerwise PC1 curves showing Gemma table rows and indentation at 45–65%.

record.verdict_notes: The superposition link is indirect. The paper never tests superposition. SAE selectivity counts lack a baseline, so V4 support is weak. V6 rows use centroid PCA, which the authors say does not establish token-level geometry. Table 2 versus text layer mismatch for Gemma-2-2B brackets (L14 vs L8). The bracket probe overfits heavily (53–57% test accuracy).

versions.untested_parts: No toy-network experiment, sparse-feature overload condition, or test of overlapping directions.
Does not test whether polysemantic neurons arise from competition for limited capacity or whether importance determines dedicated versus shared dimensions.
Does not study polysemantic neurons or alternative causes of polysemanticity.
SAE feature-family analyses cover only Gemma-2 models, not Qwen3-4B; the paper does not measure how broadly features are distributed across neurons.
Does not assess whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units of the model.
Measures PCA dimensionality of per-value centroid manifolds, not the dimensionality of individual superposed features or whether superposition occurs.

tranche.reason: Own SAE feature-family measurements in ordinal tasks provide a new-setting result on V4, although centroid PCA does not directly test V6.

source_check.notes: Section 4.1 and Figure 4's caption conflict on Qwen indentation dimensionality. Bracket probes substantially overfit; no Qwen SAE analysis is available, and subspace patching tests informational concentration rather than downstream behavioral causality.

statements.correction: Section 4.1: indentation 2–3 PCs; Gemma table rows 3–4 PCs; numeric magnitude 4–5 PCs, PC1 40–62%. Figure 4 caption: Qwen indentation and table rows collapse to 1D at middle layers. Individual superposed-feature dimensionality untested.
statements.problem: The numerical summary matches Section 4.1, but its limits_scope classification for V6 is unsupported by centroid PCA. Figure 4's caption also conflicts with the all-model indentation summary.

statements.correction: Ordinal centroid geometry varies across tasks and models. PCA of class means does not determine individual feature dimensionality or irreducibility.
statements.problem: Task-dependent centroid geometry is reported, but it does not establish coexistence of 1D and multidimensional individual superposed features.
